preamble: Spirantization of the voiced uvular stop /ɢ/ to the voiced uvular fricative [ʁ]. In Tehrani and central Iranian Persian, the merged reflex of Classical Persian /q/ (ق) and /ɣ/ (غ) is usually [ɢ], but between vowels in unstressed syllables it is realized as a fricative [ʁ] or [ɣ].

examples.note: Intervocalic and unstressed /ɢ/ is pronounced as a fricative; elsewhere it stays a stop [ɢ]. Dari and Tajik keep /q/ and /ɣ/ apart.

sources: Wikipedia (2026). Persian phonology: Consonants and allophonic variation. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Persian_phonology
